Android only allows one VPN at a time, so turning on AdShield now will disconnect your other VPN (like Surfshark).\n\nYou don\'t need to: AdShield turns on by itself as soon as Surfshark disconnects.
AdShield needs the VPN permission to block ads. Nothing leaves your phone; it filters lookups locally.

• Using Surfshark? You can switch freely. Turning Surfshark on pauses AdShield (Android allows one VPN at a time), and AdShield turns back on by itself when Surfshark disconnects. While Surfshark is on, turn on its CleanWeb feature to keep blocking ads.

• Don't turn on "Always-on VPN" for AdShield or Surfshark if you use both: it stops the other one from connecting. AdShield already turns back on after a restart by itself.

• If ads still get through, check Settings › Network › Private DNS is "Off" or "Automatic". A custom Private DNS provider skips AdShield.

• In Chrome, turn off Settings › Privacy › "Use secure DNS" for the same reason.

• If a site or app breaks, find it under "Recently blocked" and add it to "Never block".
